title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 6: scopus — do not despise the poor; 1 Cor. 1:26 parallel
pass_a_gloss: The scope of the words is this: the poor are not to be despised by us, because so far are they from being neglected by God that in the dispensation of spiritual things they are for the most part preferred to the richer; the rich, on the contrary, are not to be overly looked up to and honored with neglect of the poor, because God often sends the rich away empty while he fills the poor with goods. Not unlike this is that other place, 1 Corinthians 1:26: Not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble: but the foolish things of the world God has chosen to confound the strong, etc. The Apostle therefore shows that God has chosen more from the class of the poor, whom he would gift with both faith and heavenly inheritance, than from the number of the rich.
pass_b_english: Reply: James's point is that we must not despise the poor. Far from neglecting them, God in spiritual gifts mostly prefers them to the richer. The rich, for their part, are not to be overrated and honored while the poor are ignored — God often sends the rich away empty and fills the poor with goods. 1 Corinthians 1:26 runs the same way: not many wise by flesh, not many mighty, not many noble — God chose what the world calls foolish to shame the strong. So the Apostle shows God has chosen more from the poor, to give them faith and the heavenly inheritance, than from the rich.
source_text: Scopus verborum hic est; Pauperes non esse a nobis contemnendos, quia tantum abest ut negligantur a Deo, ut in dispensatione rerum spiritualium maximam ob partem praeferantur ditioribus: Divites e contra non esse nimis suspiciendos, & cum neglectu pauperum honorandos, quia Deus saepenumero vacuos dimittit divites, cum pauperes impleat bonis. Non absimilis huic est ille alter locus 1 Cor. i. 26. Non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobiles: Sed quae stulta sunt mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat fortia, &c. Ostendit ergo Apostolus Deum ex classe pauperum plures elegisse, quos tum fide tum hereditate caelesti donaret, quam ex numero divitum.
